titel: Shooting the Shit About "The Put Down, Pick Up Test"

einzeiler: Literary agents discuss manuscript evaluation, AI watermarks, and industry sub-stacks.
kurzfassung: Literary agents Carly Waters and CC Lyra discuss the physical and emotional experience of reading exciting new manuscripts. They examine recent news about AI text watermarks and discuss insights from industry newsletters regarding AI and submission red flags. Additionally, they share details about upcoming fall writing conferences.
stichpunkte: Discovering a great manuscript triggers a strong physical and emotional reaction, balancing urgency with careful reading.
The fear of rejection is a normal part of the process when literary agents consider offering on a project.
AI tools are increasingly implementing embedded watermarks and provenance metadata to comply with new transparency laws.
Some publishing professionals utilize custom AI models for auxiliary tasks like conference scripts and marketing copy.
The 'put-down pick-up test' helps evaluate whether a manuscript genuinely compels a reader to return to it.
Familiarity with a text's style can sometimes be confused with actual quality during the evaluation process.
Fall is the busiest season in publishing, marked by intensive submissions, meetings, and industry events.
Upcoming events include the Latinx Storytellers Conference in New York and the Surrey International Writers' Festival.

beschreibung:
Carly and CeCe are back for another Shooting the Shit, talking about that gut-level feeling that makes an agent know they’ve found something special—and why a great premise still has to deliver all the way through. The literary agents also tackle the latest publishing scams targeting writers, AI watermarking and transparency, and the growing tension around publishers using AI in parts of the business. Plus, they dig into the “put-down, pick-up test”.
